brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm at (-1,1,0) and hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf at (0,-1,0)) fill the empty spots between base cells (full bases at (0,0) and (-1,0), half base at (1,0)). Joint bolts lock the bases. check_build: meshClash clear, no rule errors.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: This configurator checks fit and mesh clearance only, not strength or load rating, so I cannot verify or claim a 50 kg rating. The build is a small 3-base structure with two drawer frames; whether it meets 50 kg needs engineering verification outside this tool.

finish.summary: Built a small hex-cluster shelf unit: three bases (two full, one half) joined by joint bolts, with two notch drawer frames set into the empty spots between them. The build passes check_build with meshClash clear and no rule errors. The 50 kg rating cannot be confirmed here, since the tool checks fit only, so that requirement is unmet/unverified.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
